clue.text: Stake controller getting more hoarse ?

definitions.meaning: the official at a casino table who collects and pays out the stakes
comparative of an adjective meaning suffering from croup, a rasping throat complaint

explanation.surface: A gambling-table official whose voice is getting rougher by the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino employee who rakes in bets has the same spelling as the comparative of croupy, meaning rasping in the throat.

clue.text: Like those ribs of beef for which one had to pay a pound?

parts.words: for which one had to pay
parts.note: something one had to pay for is said to have cost
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A butcher's rib joint that set the buyer back a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Costal is the anatomical adjective for things relating to the ribs.

clue.text: But in ___, are triumph and defeat" (Longfellow)

definitions.text: But in ___, are triumph and defeat" (Longfellow)

parts.words: But in ___, are triumph and defeat" (Longfellow)
parts.note: a line from Longfellow's poem The Ladder of St Augustine with its key word left blank to fill in

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the first-person plural reflexive pronoun from Longfellow's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Longfellow line says victory and failure lie within us, the speaker and listeners themselves.

clue.text: Ropy artist?

definitions.meaning: a rope at a boat's bow used for tying up has this name
someone who makes pictures with brushes and colours

explanation.definitionFit: A boat's mooring line at the bow shares its name with someone who makes pictures in oils or watercolour.

clue.text: Hoped for change of vestment

indicators.note: the letters of hoped are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wished for a fresh set of church robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change of' rearranges HOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is a sleeveless priestly garment worn by the Jewish high priest in the Bible.

clue.text: Weed-destructor ?

parts.note: reads like a garden herbicide, but weed is slang for tobacco, which a pipe or cigarette user burns up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' is slang for tobacco, so the person who destroys it is one who burns it in a pipe or cigarette, not a gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses tobacco burns it away, so they are a destroyer of the weed.

clue.text: Creative types are about right to cope with exam papers

indicators.note: the creators stand around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: makers are people who create things

explanation.surface: Artistic people are roped in to deal with exam scripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are about' puts R inside MAKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers or examiners who grade scripts are the people who assess them.

clue.text: Bear a knock-out in the French manner

parts.note: KO is the abbreviation for a knockout in boxing
a la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: A bear lands a knockout punch with continental flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian animal is commonly, if wrongly, called a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree-dwelling Australian marsupial is popularly called a bear, though it is not one.

clue.text: Bird makes false move into a No Go area

parts.note: red is the colour that signals stop, no go
a start is a sudden involuntary jump, a false movement

explanation.surface: A bird blunders into a forbidden zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

clue.text: He does wrong to put the last part in a proposal

indicators.note: the ending goes inside the proposal word

parts.note: an offer is something put forward for acceptance
the end is the final portion

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer slips the final clause into a marriage proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposal' suggests marriage, but it is simply something put forward; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks the law or a rule is a wrongdoer or culprit.

clue.text: A crooked fight with arrow and darts is not this

definitions.text: A crooked fight with arrow and darts is not this

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of line, so the letters of the three weapons words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest scrap involving archery and darts is anything but above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges FIGHT, ARROW and DARTS; the whole clue also defines, since something crooked is the opposite of honest and direct.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means dishonest or bent, the opposite of frank, honest and direct.

clue.text: A green journalist is turned away?

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded reporter gets sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' is the heraldic colour vert, not an eco-campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it aside, so averted means deflected or directed elsewhere.

clue.text: Refined worker follows eastern stage of the journey

indicators.note: the worker comes after the other pieces, so it sits at the end

parts.note: a leg is one section of a longer trip
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A cultured labourer tags along on an eastbound section of the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes graceful, polished, cultivated taste or manners.

clue.text: Act foolishly before the break of spring?

definitions.text: Act foolishly before the break of spring

parts.words: Act foolishly before the break of spring
parts.note: suggests silliness before the season begins, but describes turning a watch key too far so that the mainspring snaps

explanation.walkthrough: The 'spring' is a clock or watch mainspring, not the season; winding too far breaks it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a clockwork mechanism too far strains or breaks its mainspring, a foolish thing to do.

clue.text: It happens half the city is in demand for supplies

indicators.note: the first half of the city goes inside the order word

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods or stores

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters of city are taken

explanation.surface: Half the town is in need of provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: An indent is a British military and commercial term for an order for stores; 'half' takes the first two letters of city and 'is in' encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event or occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: Our system of revolution

parts.note: sounds political, but refers to the planets revolving round the Sun in the system we live in

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' is orbiting, not uprising: our planetary system is named after the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The planetary system containing Earth is named after the Sun, round which the planets revolve.

clue.text: Horrid billet, ugh ! for a Cambridge man

definitions.note: a sportsman representing Cambridge University wears its pale blue colour

indicators.note: something horrid is a mess, so the letters of billet and ugh are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A student at Cambridge complains about his awful lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrid' rearranges BILLET and UGH. Cambridge University's sporting colour is pale blue, Oxford's dark blue, so a Cambridge sportsman is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge University's colour is pale blue, so its athletes and supporters are called by that shade.

clue.text: Dogged did it when in opposition ?

definitions.meaning: in British politics opposition MPs mirror ministers as their counterparts in a shadow cabinet

explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone stealthily is to tail them; in Britain an opposition spokesperson mirrors a minister in the shadow cabinet.

clue.text: With stockings drenched

definitions.meaning: wearing hose, an old word for stockings or tights
soaked by a garden pipe spraying water

explanation.surface: Someone in stockings gets a soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose means stockings, so someone wearing them is hosed; and spraying with a hosepipe soaks a thing.

clue.text: Gets out plans, we hear, for a place in Wiltshire

indicators.note: the word for working out plans is sounded, giving a spelling with a Z

parts.note: to devise is to work out a plan

explanation.surface: Someone draws up schemes for a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals the sound-alike; Devizes is a market town in Wiltshire, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devizes is a market town in the English county of Wiltshire.

clue.text: Convey the old witch east to Dido's city

parts.note: to cart something is to carry or transport it
a hag is an ugly old woman, often a witch

explanation.surface: A crone is carried eastward to the queen's ancient capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the legendary founder and queen of the North African city in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Queen Dido founded the ancient North African city that later fought Rome.

clue.text: The custom at one's living area

parts.note: a habit is a usual practice or custom

explanation.surface: Customs observed where a person lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of a creature.

clue.text: Bakers' turnovers for teatimes

indicators.note: turning over the word bakers rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Pastries from the baker's shop served at afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnovers' looks like pastries, but signals rearranging BAKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pauses for tea in a working day are called rest periods or pauses from work.

clue.text: Obtained from a mad diver of French origin

indicators.note: the French word stands at the start, the origin of the answer

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: a mad thing is crazed and disordered, so the letters of diver are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something got from a crazy French-born diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges DIVER into RIVED, and 'origin' puts DE at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something derived is got or drawn from a source.

clue.text: The governor helps us to draw the line

definitions.text: helps us to draw the line
definitions.meaning: a straight-edged strip for drawing straight lines

explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign who governs and a straight-edged measuring stick share the same name.

clue.text: See adjusted time returned for this sort of quadrille

annotationWithheld.why: See adjusted time returned for this sort of quadrille (7): LOBSTER (the Lobster Quadrille in Alice); no parse of 'See adjusted time returned' builds the letters (LO for See leaves BSTER, which no reading of the rest gives)
annotationWithheld.clue: See adjusted time returned for this sort of quadrille

clue.text: Strange the Spanish raise such an animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words reads them from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: An odd Spaniard rears an exotic creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' reverses RUMEL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a primate found in Madagascar.

clue.text: Antipodean dancing girl ?

parts.note: looks like a description of an Australian dancer, but names the famous Australian bush song about a swagman

explanation.walkthrough: The song title reads as a girl dancing a waltz; in Australian slang it means tramping with a swag.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known Australian folk song has a title that literally reads as a girl named in a three-step dance.

clue.text: Doctor, in short, uses wrong constraint

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, that is set in a different order

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor, briefly put, abuses a restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles DR with USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion or threat used to force someone, a form of coercion.

clue.text: Labour relations

parts.note: sounds like industrial relations, but means kin; trade unionists also address each other by this word

explanation.walkthrough: Trade union members in the Labour movement call one another by the word for male siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Male siblings are family relations, and trade unionists use the same word for fellow members.
